title: Mathematical Modelling
shortDescription: Turn a real situation into equations, solve it and interpret the result.
genZNote: Word problem → equation → answer → 'does this make sense?' That last step is where marks hide.

steps.name: Build the model
steps.explanation: Write equations or inequalities (linear, proportional, break-even).

sections.heading: Typical Models
bullets: Linear cost model: Cost = fixed + rate × units. Taxi: ₹50 + ₹12/km; 8 km → ₹146.
Break-even: units = fixed cost ÷ (price − variable cost). Fixed ₹12,000, price ₹50, variable ₹30 → 600 units.
Growth models: simple vs compound; inequality constraints for budgets and capacity.
Optimisation idea: choose the best option under constraints (e.g. cheapest combination of packs).

sections.heading: Exam Tips
sections.body: Define variables explicitly; check dimensional consistency; if two unknowns, form two equations; use trial values to verify; round only at the end.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mathematical modelling represents a real-world problem with variables and equations so it can be solved and interpreted.

highYieldFacts: Always interpret the answer in context.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
